title: Interactive POC play scripts and checklist
content:
Purpose: Lightweight, reusable facilitation script + slide-outline and run checklist for customer POC workshops where the goal is to align on integration approach, validate performance SLOs (latency/cost/objectives), and leave with a clear success criteria + next steps.

Audience: Customer technical leads, product managers, infra/ops, Redwood solutions engineers, account exec (optional). 8–14 participants recommended.

Duration and structure (half-day default; can expand to full day):
- 09:00 – 09:15 — Welcome & goals (15m)
  - Facilitator: SE lead (Aisha)
  - Quick round-robin intros (name, role, 1 expectation)
  - State timebox, outcomes, and success criteria for today

- 09:15 – 09:35 — Customer context & top-3 use cases (20m)
  - Customer presents prioritized use-cases (10m)
  - Clarifying Qs (10m)
  - Goal: capture 1–2 target flows for live demo and perf validation

- 09:35 – 10:05 — Architecture alignment & constraints (30m)
  - Walk through proposed network topology, data residency, auth/KMS, and ingress/egress
  - Red flags checklist: VPC peering constraints, firewall rules, HSM requirements, compliance windows

- 10:05 – 10:25 — Hands-on demo + baseline run (20m)
  - Demo scenario: customer sample prompt(s) executed against Redwood hosted/dedicated model chosen
  - Show token counts, latency per-token, and tail latencies
  - Show cost estimate calculators for sample traffic pattern

- 10:25 – 10:40 — Break (15m)

- 10:40 – 11:20 — Interactive lab: tuning knobs & failure modes (40m)
  - Split into two small breakout groups if >8 people: "latency/cost tuning" and "reliability/fallbacks"
  - Each group given a short script to modify routing policy, quantization profile, batching window in a sandbox (SE runs changes)
  - Capture observed metric deltas and UX tradeoffs

- 11:20 – 11:40 — Runbook & rollback rehearsal (20m)
  - Walk through canary and rollback play: shift 5% traffic -> monitor + 0/1 alert triggers -> roll forward/rollback templates
  - Owner assignments created in doc

- 11:40 – 12:00 — Success criteria, action items, and close (20m)
  - Reconcile acceptance tests (functional + perf + security)
  - Confirm timeline, milestones, and responsible owners
  - Schedule follow-up checkpoint (weekly cadence recommended)

Slide outline (speaker notes included as single-line bullets per slide):
- Slide 1: Title / Workshop objective / Date / Attendees
  - Note: keep this visual minimal. Use customer logo + Redwood logo.
- Slide 2: Our shared goal (2–3 bullets)
  - Note: explicitly list acceptance tests: e.g., 95th percentile latency < 250ms for 1k RPS, avg cost/token < $0.0004, data residency in eu-west-1
- Slide 3: Target flows for demo (diagram)
  - Show sequence diagram: client -> edge -> redwood runtime -> model -> client
- Slide 4: Constraints & non-negotiables (security, compliance)
  - Note: call out items that require legal/Security follow-up (KMS policies, SOC/CIS controls)
- Slide 5: Proposed POC configuration options (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
  - Table: pros/cons, expected throughput, price ballpark, time to stand up
- Slide 6: Live baseline metrics (screenshots + numbers)
  - Note: include sample traces and per-request token breakdowns
- Slide 7: Tuning experiments (what we changed, before/after)
  - Note: include specific commands or PR links used for changes in sandbox
- Slide 8: Failure-mode scenarios & safety net (fallbacks, model variant tiers)
  - Note: show our routing policy examples and how automatic fallback kicks in
- Slide 9: Acceptance tests & success criteria checklist
  - Note: add sign-off row for each owner
- Slide 10: Next steps & timeline (coordinated milestones)
  - Note: include actions with owners and due dates

Facilitation script: (short prompts, intended to be read aloud)
- Kickoff: "Thanks everyone — quick check: what outcome would make today a success for you?"
- After customer context: "Based on those use-cases, if we could validate these two flows end-to-end with a measurable perf baseline, would that be sufficient to proceed to a POC?"
- During tuning lab: "Try to push the 95th percentile — watch the tail latency. What tradeoffs are you willing to accept for cost savings?"
- During runbook rehearsal: "If latency spikes above threshold and error rate > X, what's our immediate three-step response? Call it out and own it."

Quick facilitator checklist (pre-work + day-of):
- Pre-work for customer (send 7 days prior):
  - sample dataset or prompt corpus (size ~500–1k examples)
  - network contact and firewall/IP allow list for Redwood test agents
  - list of non-negotiable compliance items (KMS, region, logging retention)
  - point-of-contact for SRE and infra
- SE pre-work:
  - provision sandbox project and credentials (hosted/dedicated trial)
  - prepare 2 model configs (fast vs cheaper) and cost calculator output
  - smoke test demo flows and screenshot baseline traces
  - create a lightweight Confluence page with the agenda and placeholder action items
- Day-of tech checklist:
  - projector/room + remote meeting link tested
  - SSH/console access to Redwood sandbox ready
  - monitoring dashboards pre-loaded (latency, tokens, cost estimates)
  - sample prompts preloaded and validated

Common friction points + mitigation scripts:
- Customer firewall blocks our test agents -> Mitigation: ask for IP allow list pre-work or setup customer-run test container; fallback: run demo with redacted payloads via shared screen and synthetic traces
- Legal wants extra time on KMS integration -> Mitigation: propose temporary tokenization redaction during POC and schedule security deep-dive within 2 weeks
- Tail latency spikes under scale -> Mitigation: enable short-term autoscale burst and adjust batching window, document expected cost delta

POC acceptance checklist (copy into follow-up email during close):
- Functional: 5 representative prompts return correct structured outputs for 90% of test set
- Performance: 95th percentile latency < agreed threshold under target QPS (explicit number)
- Cost: projected unit cost within X% of estimate provided during workshop
- Security: data residency, KMS, and logging meet baseline commitments
- Ops readiness: rollback plan and on-call contact documented

Post-workshop follow-up template (email bullet skeleton):
- Thanks + attendees list
- One-paragraph summary of decisions made during workshop
- Copy of acceptance checklist with owner assignments and due dates
- Links to demo artifacts, baseline traces, and sandbox credentials
- Proposed date for first checkpoint (7 days) and go/no-go milestone (30 days)

Extras / improv skits (to surface hidden assumptions):
- Roleplay: "sudden peak" scenario — assign one customer PM to simulate traffic increase while an SE toggles fallback to cheaper model. Debrief: who noticed, what alerted them, what was manual vs automatic?
- Quick war game: security incident tabletop — 15-minute walk-through of incident detection to containment to customer notification.

Notes to self / TODOs for this doc:
- Add exact CLI commands for changing quantization profile (link to infra repo)
- Capture a short GIF of the baseline live run to embed on slide 6
- Add canned Slack messages for on-call notification templates

End-of-doc: Contact list for SEs who can run the lab (order by availability): Aisha Patel, Diego Martinez, Harper Nguyen.
